on_unmeasured_note: This sketch runs no participant, model or experiment and uses no human data. The figures below are the authors' statements, not measured, re-run or re-claimed here; paper_results() returns on_unmeasured. The sketch's own fixture counts are not comparable with them.
attribution: The authors' own results as stated in the arXiv abstract. Quote wording is the authors'.

claims.what: design: helpful, unhelpful and mixed advisors over repeated interactions
claims.quote: We measure how people's reliance on LLMs' advice changes across repeated interactions, varying whether the AI assistant is helpful (100% accurate), unhelpful (0% accurate), or mixed (50% accurate).
claims.on_unmeasured: not measured, re-run or re-claimed here; no human data; the sketch's fixture counts are not comparable

claims.what: trust tracks accuracy only with external feedback
claims.quote: Across 4 experiments, we find people learn to trust helpful models more than unhelpful ones (67% vs 21% of the time), but only when they receive external feedback on the models' accuracy.
claims.on_unmeasured: not measured, re-run or re-claimed here; no human data; the sketch's fixture counts are not comparable

claims.quote: Collectively, the results suggest that people may be swayed by LLM advice, even when it is consistently false, unless they have access to timely ground-truth feedback.
claims.on_unmeasured: not measured, re-run or re-claimed here; no human data; the sketch's fixture counts are not comparable

quote_policy: three abstract sentences quoted for attribution only, the ones this sketch's design rests on (C1 the three advisor accuracies, C2 trust tracking accuracy only with external feedback, C6 timely ground-truth feedback); the other abstract sentences are not quoted (the arXiv non-exclusive licence grants no reuse beyond distribution)
